sections.label: Our Teams

briefs.headline: No. 22 WVU beat No. 23 Penn State 2-1 in Morgantown
briefs.summary: Olivia Shertzer levelled from range before halftime and Sophia Nickel won it in the 68th minute. It is West Virginia's first win over Penn State since 2017.

briefs.headline: Marshall lose 4-0 at High Point on their first road trip
briefs.summary: Sabba Haghgoo scored her first collegiate hat trick and Morgan Wilcox added the fourth. The Herd took 18 shots to High Point's 16 and did not score.

briefs.headline: Cardinals hold off the Reds 10-9 after a six-run third
briefs.summary: St. Louis put up six in the third and Cincinnati could not quite come back. Strzelecki took the win at 1-1, Burke the loss at 5-5, and O'Brien his 33rd save.

sections.note: The football season starts tonight, so Chelsea, Tottenham and Liverpool carry fixtures rather than results for the last morning. Marshall's Aug. 16 home match with Ohio, the fixture between two followed teams this paper has owed since No. 1, was postponed for thunderstorms; herdzone.com would not open past the headline, so the paper reports the fixture as unresolved rather than reporting a result it could not read.

sections.label: Around the Leagues

briefs.headline: The Premier League opens with Arsenal against Coventry
briefs.summary: The champions host the promoted side at 3 p.m. ET Friday. Liverpool start the season under Andoni Iraola and Chelsea under Xabi Alonso.

briefs.headline: The Angels put 18 on Houston and deGrom shuts out Washington
briefs.summary: Los Angeles won 18-3 in Houston. Jacob deGrom and the Rangers took Washington 2-0, and Atlanta blanked the White Sox by the same score.

briefs.headline: The Aki banzuke is 10 days out and the dates are still uncited
briefs.summary: The banzuke, the rankings sheet, is due Aug. 31. The Japan Sumo Association's English pages carry no September schedule, only that every day is sold out.

sections.note: Sumo got its own search again. A Sept. 13-27 opening at Ryogoku Kokugikan is derived from the second-Sunday rule and is carried only by ticket resellers, travel sites and fan databases, which this paper does not cite - an eighth straight morning. r/Sumo could not be reached from this pipeline this morning, so the fan-forum half of the daily sweep did not run and the Japanese press half did.

notes.item: Southern flounder is closed and unlawful to possess until the Sept. 1 opening. Topsail Sound is coastal water, so Marine Fisheries governs it and not the inland digest.

sections.label: On the Water

waters.read: 350 cfs - pushy. Wadeable at the edges, not across.
waters.working: Off 755 cfs a day ago and still dropping, so the storm water is on its way out rather than blown out. At this height it is a heavy-nymph-on-the-seam problem and not a long-leader one: a weighted stonefly or a sculpin along the undercut banks and the soft edges, and stay out of the main current.

waters.near: 14 miles above R.C. Byrd Locks and Dam
waters.read: 25.7 ft and falling - normal pool. Ordinary bank access.
waters.working: Down four feet on the day and settled at pool, which puts fish back on structure. Shad are the forage: a white swimbait across the wing dams and the riprap is the first look, and the barge cuts hold fish now the colour is clearing.

waters.near: below R.C. Byrd Locks and Dam
waters.read: 28.5 ft and falling - up and pushing. Expect colour and current; fish the slack behind anything solid.
waters.working: Off seven and a half feet from yesterday, the biggest drop on the paper this morning, but still high and coloured. Debris is the hazard. The slack behind the lock wall and the rock is where to start, and a crawfish-coloured crankbait tight to the riprap is the second look.

waters.reading: Sound highs 3:15 AM at 3.0 ft and 3:56 PM at 3.9 ft at Hampstead; lows 9:34 AM at 0.6 ft and 10:34 PM at 1.2 ft.
waters.read: Fish the moving water either side of high at 3:15 AM and 3:56 PM in the sound.
waters.working: Tide before lure. The afternoon high is the bigger of the two at 3.9 feet and the only one in daylight, so the push into it is the window. Mud minnows, shrimp and finger mullet are the forage, so a soft plastic or live bait along the grass edges and the oyster bars while the water moves. Red drum, speckled trout and black drum are open; flounder is not until Sept. 1.
waters.note: Hampstead is the sound station and is the read that matters; the oceanfront station at Ocean City Beach pier runs over an hour ahead and is quoted only for a surf read. No water temperature runs today - the Wrightsville Beach gauge returned none for a fifth morning.

sections.note: USGS does not gauge the Ohio at R.C. Byrd, and the Corps tailwater data is not reachable from this pipeline. The two gauges above are the ones that bracket the dam, and neither is the tailwater.

kicker: Every water in the paper is falling again; the Williams has come off 755 cfs to 350 in a day.
